title: Johnny Dodds, Henry Zeno and George Washington
summary: Dodds played clarinet with Oliver and in parade bands and was a good reader; Zeno and George Washington drummed with Oliver and Petit.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Great drummers: who they admired and why

blocks.x: You hear Johnny Dodds much down here?
I knew you were playing with the band with Oliver. Johnny Dodds played for the parade, you know. With who? With Tuxedo, yeah. Tuxedo and the Exorcist band. Johnny Dodds was a good man.
Well, he must have been a reader.
He was. He was a reader. You tell him, Oliver was good readers. All him from his good readers.
Well, he played with so much feeling, I didn't think he was a reader, Johnny Dodds.
Oh, no, man, he's a good reader.
But he could still play good too, huh?
Good readers. So you heard Dodds Plenty down here?
Oh, yeah. And Henry, Henry Zeno was playing the drum with, with Joe Oliver. Mm-hmm. Henry Zeno, he had a good little drummer too. Oh, fast. All him from his day. Mm-hmm.
What about George Washington, the drum with the player?

Oh, yeah. George was a good drummer too. He was a young fella. Yeah. It was George's dad. He didn't, get, get the beat famous, he passed away. Who did he play with? George was playing with, he split with Buddy Petit after, after Buddy Petit split his band up. And Morris, Morris Fletcher was playing with Buddy Petit. And after, he split up and Buddy, Morris Fletcher went with Kid Ren and George, George Washington went with Buddy Petit. Oh, yeah.
